meta.note: All prices are ESTIMATES. Children prices apply to ages 3-13 in most cases. Family prices show 2 adults + 2 children. Always check official websites for current pricing and pre-book online to save.

attractions.name: Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary
attractions.description: World's oldest and largest koala sanctuary — hold a koala (extra), hand-feed kangaroos, see platypus, sheepdog shows, free-roaming wildlife. About 45 min from the CBD by river cruise or car. An essential Australian family experience.
attractions.note: Family pass (2+2) = $168. Koala hold photo extra (~$25). River cruise from CBD + entry packages available. Bring insect repellent.

attractions.name: South Bank Parklands
attractions.description: Brisbane's favourite outdoor playground — Streets Beach (patrolled artificial lagoon), Nepal Peace Pagoda, playgrounds, picnic areas, river walks, street performers. Free entry, endless fun for kids of all ages. The heart of Brisbane family life.
attractions.note: FREE. Streets Beach is completely free swimming. Paid parking at South Bank ($). Arrive early on weekends. GoMA and Museum next door.

attractions.name: Queensland Museum and Sciencentre
attractions.description: Free general admission museum with dinosaurs, Queensland wildlife, Pacific cultures, and the Sciencentre (small fee for Sciencentre). Interactive exhibits, kids' discovery centres, travelling blockbuster exhibitions. Great for curious minds.
attractions.note: Museum entry is FREE. Sciencentre entry is ~$16pp (~$65 family). Special exhibitions often have separate fees. Next to South Bank Parklands.

attractions.name: The Wheel of Brisbane
attractions.description: 60m tall observation wheel in South Bank — 360-degree views of the city, river, and mountains. Fully enclosed gondolas, light show at night. A Brisbane icon and memorable family experience.
attractions.note: Family pass (2+2) available. Night rides are spectacular with the city lights. Gondolas are air-conditioned. About 15 min ride.

attractions.name: Roma Street Parkland
attractions.description: Spectacular subtropical gardens in the heart of Brisbane — playground, water features, lake, boardwalks, free guided walks, themed gardens. A hidden oasis perfect for a family picnic or morning stroll.
attractions.note: FREE. Excellent playground. Free guided garden walks daily. Close to Roma Street Station. Bring a picnic and explore the gardens.

attractions.name: The Sciencentre
attractions.description: Interactive science centre inside Queensland Museum — hands-on exhibits, live science shows, mind-bending optical illusions. Kids can touch, play, and learn about physics, engineering, and biology.
attractions.note: Located inside Queensland Museum. Family pass ~$55. Under 5s free. Combine with the free museum galleries for a full day.

attractions.name: CityCat Ferry Ride
attractions.description: Brisbane's iconic river ferry — hop on and cruise the Brisbane River past the CBD, New Farm, South Bank, and Hamilton. Kids love the speed and views. An affordable way to see the city from the water.
attractions.note: Gocard prices shown (~$4 adult/$2 child). Cheaper with Go Explorer day pass ($10pp unlimited). A must-do Brisbane experience.

attractions.name: Mt Coot-tha Summit Lookout
attractions.description: Brisbane's best view — panoramic 360-degree city and bay views from Mt Coot-tha summit. Visit Brisbane Botanic Gardens on the way up, enjoy a coffee at the lookout cafe, spot landmarks from above.
attractions.note: FREE. About 20 min drive from CBD. Combine with the Brisbane Botanic Gardens at the base. Best at sunrise or sunset.

attractions.name: Boggo Road Gaol
attractions.description: Historic former prison turned family-friendly tourist attraction — guided tours, escape room experiences, ghost tours (older kids), and history exhibitions. An unexpectedly fascinating family outing.
attractions.note: Family pass available. Some tours (ghost tours, escape room) are extra. Not suitable for very young children. Fascinating history.

attractions.name: Story Bridge Adventure Climb
attractions.description: Climb Brisbane's iconic Story Bridge — external walk 80m above the river with 360-degree views of the city and Moreton Bay. Fully harnessed, guided, and safe. A bucket-list Brisbane experience for older families.
attractions.note: Minimum age 10 years, minimum height 130cm. Twilight and dawn climbs available. Book in advance. Not for acrophobes.

attractions.name: Eat Street Northshore
attractions.description: Massive Friday-Sunday night food market at Hamilton — 70+ food vendors from around the world, live music, fairy lights, waterfront setting. $3 entry per person (kids under 12 free). The best family night out in Brisbane.
attractions.note: $3 entry per adult, kids under 12 free. Food from ~$10-20 per dish. Live music and waterfront views. Friday-Sunday evenings only.

attractions.name: New Farm Park and Powerhouse
attractions.description: Massive riverside park with rose gardens, playgrounds, huge fig trees, riverside walks, and the Brisbane Powerhouse (free art galleries, events, markets). A favourite local family spot with plenty of space to run.
attractions.note: FREE. Powerhouse has free galleries and regular weekend markets. Huge playground by the river. CityCat ferry stop nearby.

attractions.name: City Botanic Gardens
attractions.description: Brisbane's original botanic gardens by the river — heritage trees, bamboo grove, river boardwalk, ornamental ponds. Free and tranquil escape in the city. Walking distance from the CBD and South Bank.
attractions.note: FREE. River boardwalk connects to South Bank. Great for a morning walk. Guided walks available. Wheelchair accessible.

attractions.name: Queensland Art Gallery (QAGOMA)
attractions.description: Free major art galleries at South Bank — Queensland Art Gallery and Gallery of Modern Art (GOMA). Interactive kids' exhibition spaces, free family activity guides, and world-class collections. Australia's most visited art gallery.
attractions.note: FREE entry to permanent collections. Special exhibitions sometimes have a fee. Excellent kids' activity spaces. Overlooks the river near South Bank.

attractions.name: Zone Laser Tag Brisbane
attractions.description: Indoor laser tag arena in the CBD — multi-level arena, black lights, smoke, state-of-the-art equipment. Fun for the whole family, no experience needed. Great for rainy days or birthday outings.
attractions.note: Prices per game. Package deals available for multiple games. Closed-toe shoes required. Check location for parking.

attractions.name: Slippery Slide Rock Pools (Enoggera Reservoir)
attractions.description: Natural freshwater swimming at Enoggera Reservoir — clear water, bushland setting, rope swings, rock pools. No motorized boats allowed. A secret local swimming spot. BBQ areas and walking tracks.
attractions.note: FREE. About 30 min drive from CBD. No lifeguards — swim at own risk. No facilities, BYO everything. Beautiful natural swimming.

attractions.name: Where the Wild Things Are Bookshop
attractions.description: Brisbane's best children's bookshop — story times, author events, curated kids' books, toys, and gifts. A magical space for little readers. Located in West End near South Bank.
attractions.note: FREE to browse. Regular free story time sessions. Budget $20-40 if buying books. A lovely quiet activity between outdoor adventures.

attractions.name: Brisbane River Cruise to Lone Pine
attractions.description: Scenic river cruise from the CBD to Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary — enjoy Brisbane River views, commentary, onboard cafe. Arrive right at the sanctuary jetty. A relaxing and scenic way to get to the park.
attractions.note: Includes return cruise + Lone Pine entry. Family pass available. Departs from Cultural Centre Pontoon at South Bank. Book online for best price.

attractions.name: Mission Lookout Walk (Mount Gravatt)
attractions.description: Short family-friendly bushwalk to stunning lookout over Brisbane — 2km return on a paved track, native bushland, wildflowers, panoramic views from the summit cafe. A great active family outing.
attractions.note: FREE. Paved track suitable for strollers. Summit cafe for coffee. About 20 min drive from CBD. Popular with locals for sunrise walks.
